subject: physics
title: Key ideas
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Key ideas — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.9.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Key ideas, specification section 4.9.
final_note: You worked through Key ideas — 9 specification statements.

concepts.def: One of a small number of ideas that can be used to describe the complex and diverse phenomena of the natural and man-made world. A key idea is not a detail belonging to one topic; it is a way of thinking that recurs across the whole subject.

concepts.term: Universal application of the key ideas
concepts.def: The key ideas apply everywhere in physics. They are embedded throughout the subject content, they underpin many aspects of the science assessment, and they are therefore assessed across all papers rather than in any single topic.

concepts.term: The key ideas listed in the specification
concepts.def: The key ideas in physics include: the use of models; the concept of cause and effect; ‘action at a distance’ and the related concept of the field; differences as the drivers of change; proportionality; and the expression of physical laws and models in mathematical form.

A simplified representation of a system or process, used to describe it, explain how it behaves and predict what it will do. A model does not have to be a true picture of the thing it represents in order to be useful.

A model in which matter is treated as being made of particles, whose arrangement and movement are used to explain the properties and behaviour of solids, liquids and gases. It is given in the specification as an example of the use of models.

concepts.term: Wave models of light and of sound
concepts.def: Models in which light and sound are each described as waves, so that quantities such as wavelength, frequency and speed can be used to explain how they travel and how they behave. They are given in the specification as examples of the use of models.

The idea that one physical change brings about another, so that explanations identify which is the cause and which is the effect. Examples given in the specification are the link between force and acceleration, and the link between changes in atomic nuclei and radioactive emissions.

The phenomenon of a force acting between two objects that are not touching. Electrical, magnetic and gravitational forces all act at a distance, unlike contact forces such as friction or normal contact force.

The region around an object in which another object experiences a non-contact force. The concept of the field is the key to analysing electrical, magnetic and gravitational effects: the field is a property of the object producing it and is there whether or not a second object is placed in it.

concepts.term: Differences as the drivers of change
concepts.def: Change is driven by a difference between two places or two objects, not by a large value at one place on its own. Examples given in the specification are differences between pressures, between temperatures, and between electrical potentials.

Two quantities are directly proportional when one is always the same constant multiple of the other, so that a graph of one against the other is a straight line through the origin. Proportionality is an important aspect of many models in science: weight is proportional to mass, weight = mass × gravitational field strength, W = m g; and, up to the limit of proportionality, the force on a spring is proportional to its extension, force = spring constant × extension, F = k e.

concepts.term: Physical laws and models in mathematical form
concepts.def: Physical laws and models are expressed as equations, which state exactly how the quantities are related. Writing a law mathematically allows values to be calculated, predictions to be made and the model to be tested against measurements. Rearranging an equation changes only its form, not the relationship it describes.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes what is meant by a key idea in physics?
options: An idea that runs through many topics and describes a wide range of phenomena
A rule that applies only inside the particular topic in which it is first taught
A detailed description of one particular phenomenon in great depth
A piece of background reading that is never examined on any paper
mcqs.explain: The specification states that diverse phenomena can be described in terms of a small number of key ideas.

mcqs.q: Energy is transferred from a hot drink to a cooler room, and charge flows through a lamp connected to a cell. Which key idea links these two examples?
options: A large store always empties into a store that is smaller
Both are examples of action at a distance through a field
The two examples come from separate topics and are unrelated
A difference between two places is what drives the change
mcqs.explain: A temperature difference drives the heating and a potential difference drives the charge flow.

mcqs.q: Which of these is listed in the specification as a key idea in physics?
options: That each separate area of physics is governed by its own set of rules
That differences, such as those between temperatures, drive change
That background ideas are read about but are never actually assessed
That every graph plotted in physics turns out to be a straight line
mcqs.explain: This is one of the key ideas listed in the specification.

mcqs.q: How do the key ideas relate to the assessment of GCSE Physics?
options: They are background information and are never assessed in the exam
Each key idea is assessed only within the topic that it belongs to
They are assessed only on the Higher tier papers of the whole course
They are embedded in the content and assessed across all papers
mcqs.explain: The specification states they underpin the assessment and are assessed across all papers.

mcqs.q: Why do scientists use a model such as the particle model of matter?
options: It is a scaled-down physical copy of the material being studied
It gives a simplified description that explains and predicts behaviour
It shows precisely what the particles themselves really look like
It removes every limitation from the explanation being given
mcqs.explain: A model is a simplification whose value lies in explanation and prediction.

mcqs.q: A model of matter treats particles as tiny solid spheres, although real particles are not solid spheres. What does this tell you about the model?
options: It is wrong, and so it should no longer be used in physics
It can still be useful even though it is not a true picture
It must be a physical copy of the material it represents
Particles really are solid spheres, as the model shows them
mcqs.explain: Models are judged by how well they explain and predict, not by literal accuracy.

mcqs.q: The specification gives 'the wave models of light and of sound' as an example of which key idea?
options: The idea that forces act only through direct contact
The idea that all relationships in physics are linear
The idea that differences between places drive change
The use of models to describe and explain phenomena
mcqs.explain: The wave models are listed alongside the particle model as examples of modelling.

mcqs.q: A resultant force acts on an object and the object accelerates. Which statement describes the cause and the effect correctly?
options: The acceleration is the cause; the resultant force is the effect
Neither causes the other; they simply occur at the same moment
The resultant force is the cause; the acceleration is the effect
The force is an effect of the object's mass being very large
mcqs.explain: The force acts on the object and the object responds by accelerating.

mcqs.q: A nucleus of an unstable atom changes and a radioactive emission is detected. Which statement applies the key idea of cause and effect?
options: The change in the nucleus causes the emission that is detected
The emission being detected is what makes the nucleus change
The two events are linked only because they occur together
The nucleus emits because a detector is placed close to it
mcqs.explain: The specification cites changes in atomic nuclei as the cause of radioactive emissions.

mcqs.q: A magnet attracts a steel paperclip without touching it. Which key idea does this illustrate?
options: Contact forces, because the air must touch the paperclip
Fields, but only once the paperclip is brought up close
Action at a distance, explained using the idea of a field
Proportionality, because the pull grows as distance falls
mcqs.explain: A non-contact force between separated objects is analysed using the field concept.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes what is meant by a field in physics?
options: A region that forms only once a second object is placed close by
The surface where two objects make contact and push one another apart
The path along which a force travels from one object to another
A region in which an object experiences a non-contact force
mcqs.explain: This is the field concept used to analyse electrical, magnetic and gravitational effects.

mcqs.q: A small hot metal block is placed in a large tank of cooler water. What determines the direction of the energy transfer by heating?
options: Which of the two objects stores the greater amount of energy
How hot the block is, whatever the water's temperature may be
The difference in temperature between the block and the water
The difference in mass between the block and the water in it
mcqs.explain: A temperature difference is the driver of energy transfer by heating.

mcqs.q: Air rushes out of an inflated balloon when its neck is opened. What drives this flow?
options: The high pressure of the air inside the balloon, on its own
The greater quantity of air that is stored inside the balloon
The difference in pressure between the inside and the outside
The temperature of the air inside being higher than outside
mcqs.explain: The specification gives differences between pressures as a driver of change.

mcqs.q: A graph of weight against mass for several objects is a straight line through the origin. What does this show?
options: Gravitational field strength rises as the mass increases
Weight is directly proportional to the mass of the object
Weight and mass are the same quantity in different units
Weight increases with mass but not in a fixed ratio
mcqs.explain: A straight line through the origin is exactly the condition for direct proportionality.

mcqs.q: What must a graph show if two quantities are to be directly proportional?
options: A straight line that passes through the origin
A straight line, wherever it happens to cross an axis
A line whose gradient increases steadily as it rises
A smooth curve rising steadily from left to right
mcqs.explain: Both conditions are required for direct proportionality.

mcqs.q: A spring extends 40 mm when a force of 8.0 N is applied. Force and extension remain directly proportional. What is the extension when the force is 12 N?
options: 60 mm
27 mm
44 mm
48 mm
mcqs.explain: The force is multiplied by 1.5, so the extension is 40 mm × 1.5 = 60 mm, with k unchanged.

mcqs.q: What does it mean to say that a physical law is expressed in mathematical form?
options: The symbols are shorthand labels and carry no relationship
The equation works only in the exact order it is written
The relationship between the quantities is written as an equation
The law is usable only when every value is already known
mcqs.explain: An equation states exactly how the quantities in the law are related.

mcqs.q: The equation F = m a is rearranged to a = F ÷ m. What effect does this rearrangement have?
options: It changes the relationship so acceleration now causes force
None; it states the same relationship in a different form
It makes the symbols stand for different physical quantities
It shows that acceleration must be measured before force
mcqs.explain: Rearranging changes the form of an equation, not the relationship it expresses.

specSource: AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification; section 4.9 Key ideas
